task_instance: Attempt to execute one minimal cli-exercise 'behavior case' via the skill's mandated flow: obtain a ready preflight receipt and approved contract, launch the subject CLI (e.g. a trivial `gh` invocation) through the Go helper's `run` command with checksum verification of the executable, observe terminal state through the Tuistory client, record a session manifest per references/recording-sessions.md, and capture startedAt/finishedAt metadata for a single setup/exercise/validation case.
blocker_detail: The skill is not a generic CLI-automation recipe; it is the internal execution layer for a proprietary 'cli-exercise' framework. It requires: (1) a specific 'Go helper' binary exposing a `run` command that consumes a contract + preflight receipt and enforces checksum verification of the exact approved executable, (2) a 'controller' interpreter following references/controllers.md's declarative format, (3) a Node 'Tuistory' adapter that provides a mechanical terminal boundary/client for reading actual terminal state and issuing revision-checked actions, and (4) a session-manifest/shared-state convention per references/recording-sessions.md, plus the paired cli-exercise-evidence module. None of this tooling exists on the workstation -- only generic go, node, python3 and gh binaries are installed (verified with `which`/`go version`/`node --version`), and a filesystem-wide search (`find / -iname '*tuistory*'`, `find / -iname '*cli-exercise*'`) found no such runtime, binary, or library anywhere outside of unrelated benchmark scratch files that merely share the skill's name. Building this framework from scratch (contract/receipt schema, checksum-gated launcher, terminal-state observer with revision semantics, controller interpreter, manifest recording) is out of scope for a 15-minute exercise and, per the skill, is also explicitly the wrong approach ('Node only supplies the mechanical Tuistory boundary. It must not replace Go's contract checks...') -- i.e. the skill assumes this infrastructure is already provided by the (absent) cli-exercise product, not something the agent should reimplement ad hoc.
evidence: Ran from work directory: `which go node python3 gh` -> /usr/local/go/bin/go, /opt/node22/bin/node, /usr/local/bin/python3, /usr/local/bin/gh (generic tools present). `go version` -> go1.24.7 linux/amd64; `node --version` -> v22.22.2 (generic runtimes only, not the skill's specific 'Go helper'/'Tuistory adapter'). `find / -iname '*tuistory*'` and `find / -iname '*cli-exercise*' -not -path '/home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/*'` returned only unrelated benchmark scratchpad directories/files from other runs of this same evaluation harness (paths like .../scratchpad/exec/cli__cli__cli-exercise-run, .../rt_dry/packs/ce_rt/cli__cli__cli-exercise.json), none of which are an actual executable runtime; no cli-exercise Go binary, contract/receipt files, controller files, or Tuistory adapter package were found anywhere on the machine. The skill document itself (read at /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/benchmark/ce_sources/cli__cli__cli-exercise-run/SKILL.md) references three other required docs (../../references/runtime-interface.md, controllers.md, recording-sessions.md) and a sibling skill (../cli-exercise-evidence/SKILL.md) that were out of scope to read per task instructions, but even the SKILL.md alone makes clear the flow depends on a preexisting, checksum-verified, purpose-built execution/recording product rather than on any combination of stock CLI tools. No deliverable (a completed case manifest with a real recorded terminal session) could be produced.
